thread:
alex: FYI customer Sam (cust-sam) just escalated — Private deployment in eu-west is seeing intermittent API 502/504s and failed TLS handshakes when routing via their DX link. Says it started ~2h ago.

ingrid: Oof. Any changes on their side? config/keys?

cust-sam: Not on our side — we rotated no certs. We did deploy a routing change to test failover, but rolled back. Errors started after that, might be related.

matt: Can you share traceroutes + tcpdump from their app host to the private endpoint? Also need ipsec status on their VPN / BGP session state for DX.

cust-sam: Attaching results: traceroute to private-api.redwood.internal -> shows first hop to their DX appliance then times out after 3 hops. tcpdump shows SYNs to vip but SYN/ACK sometimes from different next-hop.

alex: That smells like asymmetric routing / route leak. If their DC accidentally advertised a default or large aggregate, traffic could be leaving via DX and returning a different path — breaks stateful NAT / IPSec esp. for TLS.

oncall-bot: @netops assigned incident NET-2318 to investigate peering path (priority P1).

netops: Looking at BGP adjacency from our side — I see a new prefix 0.0.0.0/0 being advertised from their edge at 17:08 UTC, with MED 100. That would explain return path biasing to on-prem.

ingrid: Did they advertise that into route-reflector by mistake? Can they show BGP config (no secrets) or RIB before/after?

cust-sam: Confirmed — an automated policy test pushed a temporary 0.0.0.0/0 announce for failover at 17:06 then removed at 17:18. We thought it only applied to some ASes but looks like it propagated.

matt: Okay, so timeline matches. That route leak would make our private endpoints reachable via on-prem path. Two consequences: (1) egress allowlist or firewall rules on their side drop return packets if source IPs don't match expected egress, and (2) IPSec SAs see traffic from unexpected outer IP ->ESP policy mismatch -> packets dropped. Also TLS renegotiation failures if session pinned to different IP.

alex: Also check DNS split-horizon — are clients resolving private-api.redwood.internal to an IP that exists only on our peering side vs the on-prem path? If the customer uses split-horizon and the leaked route shifts the path, their resolver might get inconsistent answers.

cust-sam: They use internal DNS. We verified records, but our resolver sometimes returned the private VIP and sometimes the on-prem-rewritten address during the leak window.

netops: Repro steps I used from our edge: 1) bgp table dump showed /0 from AS64501 at 17:08. 2) built full traceroute: traffic left via dx01 -> onprem-router -> returned via internet transit to eu-west -> hit API nodes with different src. 3) captured ESP logs: ipsec_sa_replay errors and 'Bad SPI' on some packets.

ingrid: Temporary mitigation: ask them to withdraw the /0 and clear iBGP on reflectors (they already removed it). On our side, we should pin sessions to the canonical peering path for private deployments until BGP converges (deploy a temporary inbound route-map to prefer our prefix origin?).

matt: Also recommend they flush DNS caches and ensure their resolver doesn't have split responses. We'll roll a traffic gate for that customer's private model (rate-limit and stick to original peering IPs) to avoid TLS sessions bouncing.

cust-sam: We've withdrawn the announce and flushed caches. We're still seeing a few 502s — maybe stale flows. Any commands you'd like us to run?

alex: Run these and paste outputs: 1) ip route get <vip> 2) ipsec statusall 3) tcpdump -nni eth0 host <vip> and capture 100 packets.

cust-sam: Pasted ip route -> shows sometimes next-hop via dx01, sometimes via internet-gw. ipsec statusall shows a mismatch count of ~140 and some SAs in aging. tcpdump attached — you can see SYN then duplicate ACKs from different src.

netops: That confirms asymmetry. Post-convergence checklist: 1) confirm /0 withdrawn on their RIB globally (we see it's gone now), 2) clear any static pinned routes on their routers, 3) wait for BGP timers (convergence ~30-60s), 4) clear IPSec SAs on both ends to force rekey with new path, 5) have them flush DNS and restart app pool to drop pinned TLS sessions.

ingrid: On our infra side, I'm going to add a temporary per-customer fallback route to prefer our direct peering IPs for 24h. Also enable extra logging for TLS handshake error rates for that tenant.

alex: Noted. I'll coordinate with infra to keep the traffic gate live until customer confirms.

cust-sam: Following your steps now — we cleared SAs and restarted services. Error rate dropping. Thanks, team.

matt: One postmortem item: recommend they limit automated test announces (esp /0) from CI — add a sandbox AS path or a validation step so reflectors filter accidental aggregates.

ingrid: Agreed. We'll follow up with them on hardening BGP policies and also document this in runbook: "route-leak -> IPSec/TLS impact".

alex: Closing loop: last 30m looks stable. I'll leave NET-2318 open for postmortem items. :white_check_mark:
